# 0 · Setup

```{r package-setup}
# Data wrangling and visualisation
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(gt)
library(patchwork)

# Data import
library(midphysac)
```

## Variables

```{r variables}
# A2PA used as the sole predictor for the whole poster
x <- "A2PA"

# Outcomes compared between A2PA groups
Y <- c(
  "Age", "MMSE", "Education",
  "Current PA (WHO)", "Current PA (excl. walking, chores)", "Current PA (excl. walking, chores, gardening)",
  "SA",
  "RAVLR-DR", "z(RAVLT-DR)",
  "TMT-B", "z(TMT-B)",
  "BNT-30", "z(BNT-30)", "Animal naming", "z(Animal naming)",
  "GDS-15", "Prob. depression", "GAI-SF", "Prob. anxiety", "FAQ",
  "Mental activities",
  "BMI", "Subj. health", "Smoking", "Alcohol", "Hypertension", "Diabetes"
)
```

## Data

```{r data-import}
# NOTE: data live in a freeze artifact at OSF
raw_data <- midphysac::read_poster_data()

# NOTE: data are trimmed at A2PA < 4 for this analysis
df <- filter(raw_data, A2PA <= "Active")
```

---

# 1 · The sample (row 1, column 2)

```{r sample-palette}
# Poster palette. Athlete / Enthusiast / Active carry the group colours used in
# every panel; everything below the third level is greyed to mark exclusion.
pal  <- c(Athlete = "#22415C", Enthusiast = "#D19A2E", Active = "#3F8E8C")
grey <- "#6E7C8C"
ink  <- "#1E2833"
hair <- "#C3D2DE"

# Row fills are the same hues mixed 15 % over white. col2rgb() returns colours
# in COLUMNS, rgb() wants them in ROWS, hence the transpose.
tint <- function(x, p = 0.15) {
  grDevices::rgb(t(p * grDevices::col2rgb(x) + (1 - p) * 255), maxColorValue = 255)
}
```

```{r sample-table}
# All five A2PA levels, including the two that the analyses exclude.
sample_rows <-
  raw_data |>
  summarise(
    N    = n(),
    Age  = sprintf("%.1f (%.2f)", mean(Age,  na.rm = TRUE), sd(Age,  na.rm = TRUE)),
    MMSE = sprintf("%.1f (%.2f)", mean(MMSE, na.rm = TRUE), sd(MMSE, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .by  = A2PA
  ) |>
  arrange(A2PA) |>
  mutate(A2PA = as.character(A2PA))

# Accent per row: palette for the analysed levels, grey for the rest.
n_keep <- length(pal)
accent <- c(unname(pal), rep(grey, nrow(sample_rows) - n_keep))
fills  <- tint(accent)

# Education is stated in the note rather than given a column.
edu_range <-
  df |>
  summarise(higher = mean(Education == "higher", na.rm = TRUE), .by = A2PA) |>
  pull(higher) |>
  range()

sample_rows
```

```{r sample-gt}
tab_sample <-
  sample_rows |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::cols_label(A2PA = "A2PA identity", N = "N", Age = "Age", MMSE = "MMSE") |>
  gt::cols_align("left",  columns = A2PA) |>
  gt::cols_align("center", columns = c(N, Age, MMSE)) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_text(color = grey, weight = "bold"),
    locations = gt::cells_column_labels()
  )

# Row-wise colour coding. A left rule in the full-strength hue carries the code
# even in greyscale; the fill is a quiet second cue.
for (i in seq_len(nrow(sample_rows))) {
  tab_sample <-
    tab_sample |>
    gt::tab_style(
      style = list(
        gt::cell_fill(color = fills[i]),
        gt::cell_text(color = if (i <= n_keep) ink else grey)
      ),
      locations = gt::cells_body(rows = i)
    ) |>
    gt::tab_style(
      style = list(
        gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
        gt::cell_borders(sides = "left", color = accent[i], weight = gt::px(10))
      ),
      locations = gt::cells_body(columns = A2PA, rows = i)
    )
}

tab_sample <-
  tab_sample |>
  gt::tab_source_note(gt::md(sprintf(
    "**Sample**  
    Women aged over 80, free of cognitive or functional impairment. %d assessed in total. Age and MMSE presented as M (SD) in years and points out of 30, respectively.",
    nrow(raw_data)
  ))) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(gt::md(sprintf(
    "**Excluded**  
    The %d least active identities (grey) are too sparse for stratum-level estimates and are left out of every analysis, leaving *N* = %d.",
    nrow(sample_rows) - n_keep, nrow(df)
  ))) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(gt::md(sprintf(
    "**Education**  
    Comparable across the analysed identities, with %.0f–%.0f %% completing higher education.",
    100 * edu_range[1],
    100 * edu_range[2]
  ))) |>
  # html() rather than md() here: this note needs line breaks and inline markup
  # together, and raw HTML in a markdown note is not guaranteed to survive.
  gt::tab_source_note(gt::html(paste0(
    "<strong>Measures</strong><br>",
    "&#127939; <em>Physical activity</em>: COBRA-B, scored at three nested definitions.<br>",
    "&#129504; <em>Cognition</em>: RAVLT delayed recall, TMT-B, BNT-30, animal naming; ",
    "SuperAging by Northwestern criteria.<br>",
    "&#129658; <em>Health</em>: <em>mental</em> GDS-15, GAI, FAQ &middot; ",
    "<em>subjective</em> self-rated health &middot; ",
    "<em>metabolic</em> BMI, smoking, alcohol, diabetes, hypertension."
  ))) |>
  gt::tab_options(
    table.font.names               = "Helvetica Neue",
    table.font.size                = gt::px(30),
    table.font.color               = ink,
    table.width                    = gt::pct(100),
    table.border.top.style         = "none",
    table.border.bottom.style      = "none",
    table_body.hlines.style        = "none",
    column_labels.font.size        = gt::px(27),
    column_labels.font.weight      = "bold",
    column_labels.text_transform   = "uppercase",
    column_labels.border.top.style = "none",
    column_labels.border.bottom.color = hair,
    column_labels.border.bottom.width = gt::px(2),
    data_row.padding               = gt::px(12),
    source_notes.font.size         = gt::px(26)
  )

tab_sample
```
